series.name: Semantic Relationships
series.description: Maps direct, hierarchical, causal, and dynamic connections between entities identified in Series 2.

open_ended.text: What direct associations exist between entities? Which entities reference, point to, or are linked to which others?

follow_up_choices.text: Sparse — fewer associations than entities; most entities are isolated
Moderate — roughly one association per entity on average
Dense — entities form a richly connected web
Clustered — dense connections within groups, sparse between groups

open_ended.text: What is the nature or type of each association? Is it a use, creation, ownership, or communication link?

follow_up_choices.text: Single type — all associations are of the same nature
2–3 distinct relationship types (e.g., owns, produces, references)
4–7 distinct relationship types covering different interaction modes
8+ relationship types — rich relational vocabulary needed

open_ended.text: What parent-child, containment, or hierarchical relationships exist? Which entities are within, belong to, or are part of others?

follow_up_choices.text: No hierarchy — all entities are peers with no containment structure
Shallow hierarchy (1–2 levels) — simple containment chains
Deep hierarchy (3+ levels) — multi-level nesting
DAG structured — entities form a directed acyclic graph with multiple parents

open_ended.text: What inheritance, specialization, or generalization relationships exist? Which entities are kinds of other entities?

follow_up_choices.text: No inheritance — each entity is unique in its type
Simple inheritance — a few parent types with child specializations
Polymorphic hierarchy — entities can serve as multiple types simultaneously
Trait-based — entities pick capabilities from a shared set of traits

open_ended.text: What causal, temporal, or triggering relationships exist? Which entities cause changes in, or are triggered by, others?

follow_up_choices.text: No causal links — entities change independently
Direct causation — entity A creates or changes entity B in a predictable chain
Event-driven — state changes propagate as events through the network
Feedback loops — entities can influence each other in circular patterns

open_ended.text: What dependency chains, prerequisites, or ordering constraints exist? Must some entities exist before others can be created or used?

follow_up_choices.text: No ordering constraints — entities are independent
Simple chain — a linear sequence of prerequisites
Branching dependencies — a DAG of ordered entity relationships
Cyclic dependencies — entities depend on each other (requires careful management)

open_ended.text: What rules govern how relationships can change? Can associations be created, deleted, or modified at any time, or are there restrictions?

follow_up_choices.text: Freely mutable — relationships can change at any time with no restrictions
State-gated — relationships can only change when entities are in certain states
Immutable after creation — relationships are set once and cannot change
Versioned — relationship changes create new versions rather than modifying in place

open_ended.text: How do relationships compose or chain across entities? Can indirect relationships be inferred from direct ones?

follow_up_choices.text: No composition — only direct relationships matter
Transitive — some relationship types imply transitive chains
Composable — relationships can be combined according to specific rules
Weighted/typed composition — chains have strength or type that affects meaning
